_comment: The Telemetry screen's model, shared verbatim by both front-ends (macOS TelemetryView.swift, Linux telemetryview.py) and by the shared math in DiplomatCore/Telemetry.swift + diplomat_runtime/telemetry.py. Titles, blurbs, glyphs and colours live here so the two screens cannot describe the same number differently; the numbers themselves come from the ledger at ~/.diplomat/pr-monitor/<ledgerFile>.
_gatheringComment: A poll runs every 3 minutes, which is far finer than any chart here needs and would grow the ledger by ~70KB a day. One sample every 15 minutes still leaves ~1300 usable intervals across a fortnight to price the rate-limit window from, and keeps two months of history under a megabyte. retainDays MUST be at least the longest range above, or the screen would offer a lookback the ledger no longer covers; the file is rewritten to that horizon once it passes maxLedgerBytes.
_quotaFreshnessComment: quotaFreshSamples = how many missed samples a quota reading survives before it stops being an answer to "what is left right now" — the silence the chart draws through, and the age past which the headline reads "—". One number for both, or a broken line ends up captioned with a figure. Four intervals is an hour: enough to ride out a few missed polls, and on a machine whose probe is answering it never fires at all.
_rangesComment: The lookback the screen offers. 14 days is the default: a week is short enough that one quiet weekend halves every average, and 30+ smooths out exactly the regression you opened the screen to find. bucketHours is how wide one bar of the finished-work chart is at that range, picked so every range draws 28-42 bars — the band where a bar is still thick enough to see and there are still enough of them to have a shape. Each divides its range exactly, so no bar covers a shorter stretch of time than the ones beside it and their heights compare.
_seriesComment: steps = how many instants the pending-over-time series is sampled at across the whole range (evenly spaced, the last one being 'now'); bins = histogram buckets for the per-task spread. Both are fixed so the two platforms draw the same chart from the same ledger. The spread is up to TWO histograms — tasks against the 7-day window, and those the ledger's 5-hour readings covered against the 5-hour one — sharing one set of bin edges, so a bin is the same slice of the x axis for both and the two can be read against each other.
_confidenceComment: A normal-approximation interval on the MEAN (z x sd / sqrt(n)), not a prediction interval for one task — the shaded band answers 'where does the average sit', which is what a budget is planned against. z is the two-sided normal quantile for the level.
_minSampleComment: Below this many finished tasks the spread is noise, and the screen says so instead of drawing a curve through three points.

metrics.title: Limit per task
metrics.blurb: Mean share of the 7-day rate-limit window one auto-task consumes.

metrics._comment: The card, which charts both windows at once — tasks priced against each — so it is named for both. The two entries below are the SERIES: their titles name the two windows in the figures printed under the chart, and their colours the bars. The 5-hour series holds only tasks started while the ledger still had readings of that window. A task is a big slice of a 5-hour window and a sliver of a week, so the two humps sit far apart on the shared axis.
metrics.title: Spread
metrics.blurb: Tasks priced against each rate-limit window, as a histogram with a confidence interval on its mean. The 5-hour series counts only tasks started while the ledger still had readings of that window.

metrics.title: 5-hour
metrics.blurb: Share of the 5-hour rate-limit window an auto-task consumed, for tasks its readings covered.

metrics.title: 7-day
metrics.blurb: Share of the 7-day rate-limit window one auto-task consumes.

metrics._comment: Not derived from anything: the OAuth usage probe reports what is left of the 7-day rate-limit window, every sample, and this is that reading drawn as it was measured, over the 5-hour readings older samples carry. The headline is the 7-day figure, and this tint is both the card's and the 5-hour fill's. The percentages elsewhere on the screen are per-TASK, which needs the window priced in tokens first (see calibrate) — this one does not.
metrics.title: Rate limit left
metrics.blurb: What is left of the 7-day rate-limit window, as measured every sample. The shaded fill is the 5-hour window, wherever the ledger holds readings of it; the usage probe reports the week alone.

metrics._comment: The card head, which charts both series at once — so it is named for both. The two entries below are the SERIES: their titles key the legend and their colours the fills.
metrics.title: Owed work
metrics.blurb: Work the monitors had found but that no agent had started yet.

metrics.title: Auto-reviews
metrics.blurb: Reviews the monitor had found but not yet started, over time.

metrics.title: Conflict fixes
metrics.blurb: Conflict fixes the monitor had found but not yet started, over time.

metrics._comment: The delivered half of a pair: 'Owed work' charts what the monitors found and nobody had taken, this what actually finished. Bucketed by when a task ENDED, so a run spanning two buckets is one delivery counted in the bucket it ended in — and a task the mesh placed on a peer counts, because it was delivered, even though its cost is the peer's and stays out of the per-task figures.
metrics.title: Finished work
metrics.blurb: Auto-tasks that finished, counted in equal buckets across the lookback.

metrics.title: Time to finish
metrics.blurb: Mean wall-clock from an agent starting to its exit.

metrics.title: Time to start
metrics.blurb: Mean wait from the monitor first seeing the work to an agent taking it.

metrics._comment: Named for what it actually measures: the split is by the cwd each Claude turn ran in, so it counts every session in the monitored repo — the agents this applet dispatches, and the operator's own work in the same checkout. Calling it 'Diplomat' would claim an attribution the cwd cannot make.
metrics.title: Spent on this repo
metrics.blurb: Share of this machine's Claude tokens spent in the repo the agents work in (Settings → repo root, and its worktrees) rather than everywhere else.
